title: Three Student Questions to Start (or Spark) Your School Year
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Stuart describes a first-day-of-school writing activity built around three short-answer questions, each engineered to surface a different one of his "Five Key Beliefs" motivational framework. One question probes Effort/Efficacy by asking students to recall a hard skill they've mastered, one probes Value by asking about the most interesting moment in world history, and one probes Credibility by asking students to describe a great teacher. He shares sample student responses to illustrate the range and candor the prompts elicit. The larger point is that the questions do double duty: they give the teacher fast, low-lift insight into each student's inner world, and they give students a moment of reflection that primes beliefs Stuart considers foundational to motivation. He recommends the activity for the first day of the year but notes it works equally well as a mid-semester reset.
points: Ties three quick short-answer prompts directly to the Effort/Efficacy, Value, and Credibility legs of the Five Key Beliefs framework, turning a simple icebreaker into deliberate belief-cultivation.
Nine sentences of student writing gives the teacher fast, low-lift insight into each student's inner world without a lengthy diagnostic.

Sample answers (e.g., a student's account of memorizing country flags or overcoming years of math struggle) show the prompts reliably surface concrete, specific evidence of prior effort students can build on.
Recommends the activity as reusable beyond day one - any day of the semester when a change of pace or a motivational reset is needed.
